_readme: Performance Max for lejhojtaler.dk. Deploy with:
READ THIS BEFORE ENABLING THE CAMPAIGN.
PMax always runs smart bidding, so it optimises toward whatever is marked
primary in Tools > Conversions. As of 2026-08-16 that includes six GA4
events with category PURCHASE: page_view, session_start, user_engagement,
first_visit, scroll and form_start. Over the last 30 days they produced 180
of the account's 181 'conversions'; the real purchase action produced 1.
Enable this campaign against that goal set and Google will spend 1000 kr/day
buying pageviews. Set those six to Secondary first, leave only 'purchase'
Final-URL expansion cannot be switched off any more. Google removed
campaign.url_expansion_opt_out from the API, so PMax will always send some
traffic to pages it picks itself. The upside is that the occasion pages not
/julefrokost, /konfirmation) can earn traffic on their own. The downside is
that /lejevilkaar and /privatlivspolitik are equally eligible — hence the
url_exclusions list, which is the only remaining control.

campaign.name: Lejhøjtaler — Performance Max
campaign._bidding_note: No target_cpa on launch — a tCPA before the campaign has conversion history just throttles delivery. Add one after ~30 real bookings.
campaign._url_exclusions_note: Negative webpage criteria, matched as 'URL contains'. Keeps expansion off the legal pages, the admin app and the English tree — the campaign only carries Danish assets, so an English landing page would read as a mismatch. /book is deliberately NOT excluded: the 'Priser og booking' sitelink points there on purpose.

targeting._geo_note: The search campaign targets the city constant 'Copenhagen' (1005010), which is Københavns Kommune only — one reason it can only spend 40 kr/day. 40 km from København K reaches Roskilde, Køge, Hillerød and Helsingørs opland, all within reach of the 495 kr delivery. PRESENCE keeps out the 'soundboks leje odense' clicks visible in the search-term report.
